chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from one of his companions, raising it (to the Imam), said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Two things are corrective; if either enters the stomach of a person who is spoilt (ill), it corrects it. And two things are spoilers; if either enters the stomach of a person who is sound (healthy), it spoils it. The two correctives are the pomegranate and lukewarm water, and the two spoilers are cheese and dried meat (jerk).'
ai.seo_question: What are the two foods that cure illness and the two that cause it according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the medicinal properties of common foods, highlighting pomegranate and lukewarm water as restorative agents for the ill, while identifying cheese and dried meat (jerky) as detrimental to the healthy. This classification reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of integrating prophetic medicine (*al-Tibb al-Nabawi*) with clinical observation, emphasizing the balance between dietary intake and bodily constitution. The specific mention of 'jerky' in the chapter title underscores the historical context of food preservation and its perceived impact on digestion and vitality in early Islamic society.
